Fixed (#2). Root cause: in rrule._iter() the count was copied to a local and only decremented inside `if count:` guards — since 0 is falsy, `count=0` never terminated, so the rule ran to year 9999 instead of yielding nothing. Added an early return in `_iter` when `self._count == 0` (sets `_len = 0`). Verified: list(rrule(DAILY, count=0, dtstart=...)) == [], .count() == 0, works via rrulestr/rruleset/caching; count=1 and count=2 unchanged. Test suite: dateutil/test/test_rrule.py 542 passed; full dateutil/test 1064 passed, 43 skipped — same as before the change.

Fixed (#4): rrule.__str__ was joining the parts without the RFC2445 property token, producing e.g. 'DTSTART:19970902T090000\nFREQ=YEARLY;COUNT=3'. It now appends 'RRULE:' (so the output is 'DTSTART:19970902T090000\nRRULE:FREQ=YEARLY;COUNT=3'), matching the method's docstring and rrulestr's RRULE: handling. Round-trip through rrulestr verified across 105 rule configurations; test_rrule.py 542 passed, full suite 1064 passed / 43 skipped (unchanged).
